question.prompt:
Each of the twenty dots on the graph below represents one of Sarah’s classmates. Classmates who are friends are connected with a line segment. For her birthday party, Sarah is inviting only the following: all of her friends and all of those classmates who are friends with at least one of her friends. How many classmates will not be invited to Sarah’s party?

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Sarah invites classmates who can be reached from her by one or two friendship segments. Count these classmates in two passes, counting each dot only once.

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

First mark the \(9\) dots connected directly to Sarah. Next inspect the connections from those original friends and mark any previously unmarked dots. This adds two dots attached to the lower-left friend, one just to the right of the lowest direct friend, one below the rightmost direct friend, and one immediately beyond the upper-right friend along the outer chain. These are \(5\) additional classmates.

Every invited classmate belongs to one of these two groups. Counting only previously unmarked dots prevents counting someone twice, even when several friends connect to that person. Thus the number not invited is
\[
20-9-5=\boxed{6}.
\]
The uninvited classmates are the three dots in the detached triangle, the isolated dot, and the bottommost and far-right dots, which each require three friendship connections from Sarah. The answer is \(\boxed{D}\).
solutions.title: Follow two friendship connections
